title: Widest Gap Between Different Colors
statement:
A street has n houses in a row. House i is painted color colors[i]. At least two houses have different colors.

Return the largest distance j − i over all pairs i < j with colors[i] !== colors[j].

examples.why: The only house that differs is in the middle, and it is 2 away from either end.
Pairing the first house with the farthest different one gives 4 − 0 = 4. Pairing the last house instead gives 6 − 1 = 5. You must try both ends.
The two houses differ, so the whole street counts.

constraints: At least two houses have different colors
hints: The best pair surely uses one of the two end houses. Why?

Take a best pair (i, j). If colors[0] differs from colors[j], the pair (0, j) is at least as wide. If colors[n − 1] differs from colors[i], so is (i, n − 1). If neither, the two ends have the colors of j and i, which differ, so (0, n − 1) itself is valid.
Answer = max(farthest j with colors[j] ≠ colors[0], (n − 1) − nearest i with colors[i] ≠ colors[n − 1]).

explain.intuition:
Take a best pair (i, j). If the first house differs from house j, then (0, j) is at least as wide. If the last house differs from house i, then (i, n − 1) is. If neither holds, the first house has house j's color and the last has house i's, and those differ, so the whole street (0, n − 1) is a valid pair. Either way, some best pair touches an end of the street.

So you only need two scans. From the right, find the farthest house that differs from the first one. From the left, find the nearest house that differs from the last one. The wider of the two gaps wins.
steps: Walk j down from n − 1 until colors[j] ≠ colors[0]. Candidate 1 is j.
Walk i up from 0 until colors[i] ≠ colors[n − 1]. Candidate 2 is n − 1 − i.
pitfalls: Checking only the first house. In [5, 3, 3, 3, 3, 5, 5] that gives 4 instead of 5.
Assuming the ends differ from each other and returning n − 1 right away.

solutions.title: Check every pair
solutions.idea: Compare every pair of houses and keep the widest pair whose colors differ.

solutions.title: Anchor at one end
solutions.idea: Some best pair uses the first or the last house. Scan inward from the opposite end for the first house that differs.

followups: Return the widest gap for each color c: the widest pair where one house has color c and the other does not.
Houses are on a circle, so distance is the shorter way around. Does the end-anchoring argument still hold?
